classification.difficultyReason: Express three original dimensions using the resulting cube edge, expand a volume difference, solve the resulting quadratic and reject an inadmissible root.

content.prompt:
While wrapping his son’s Christmas present, which is in the shape of a rectangular box, a parent notices that if the length of the box was increased by 2 cm, the width increased by 3 cm and the height increased by 4 cm, the box would become a cube and its volume would be increased by $1207\text{ cm}^3$.

Find the length of the edge of the resulting cube and the dimensions of the box.

answer.short:
Cube edge: $13\text{ cm}$. Box: $11\text{ cm}\times10\text{ cm}\times9\text{ cm}$.

Express the box dimensions using the cube edge and equate the increase in volume to $1207\text{ cm}^3$.
answer.worked:
Let the cube edge be $x$ cm. The box has length $(x-2)$ cm, width $(x-3)$ cm and height $(x-4)$ cm, so $x>4$.

$$\begin{align*}x^3-(x-2)(x-3)(x-4)&=1207\\x^3-(x^2-5x+6)(x-4)&=1207\\x^3-(x^3-9x^2+26x-24)&=1207\\9x^2-26x+24&=1207\\9x^2-26x-1183&=0\\9x^2-117x+91x-1183&=0\\9x(x-13)+91(x-13)&=0\\(x-13)(9x+91)&=0\end{align*}$$

By the null factor law, $x=13$ or $x=-\frac{91}{9}$. Since $x>4$, the cube edge is $13$ cm.

The original box has length $13-2=11$ cm, width $13-3=10$ cm and height $13-4=9$ cm.

Check: $13^3-11\times10\times9=2197-990=1207\text{ cm}^3$.
